items.title: Waldren "Frog" Joseph Interview, 1961-07-10
items.q: Up, say in New York, if you'd ask Eddie Conner or somebody to play a waltz, they'd be insulted.

ctx.x: If you're going to learn music, do it just like anything else. If you was a carpenter you couldn't tell me you couldn't build a two-story house. You couldn't build just one story. So if you're going to play music, try to play all type of music if you've got to make a living out. And I never will forget that. So that's why, I mean, I try to play all the music. I mean, I love the New Orleans music, but sometimes I can't make a living out. And that's all I can do is play the music.

I know down here though, the dancers, they always, that impressed me too when I first came down, they always played waltzes and other kinds of pieces. Up, say in New York, if you'd ask Eddie Conner or somebody to play a waltz, they'd be insulted. They'd say, get out of here, this is a jazz band. But down here they play all the guys. That's one thing you've got to give to the New Orleans musicians.
They try to satisfy, you know, the guests, you know.
